When these weird artworks appeared.Malevich's Black Square: Kazimir Malevich's painting is a black square on white, which he called the zero point of painting.
When these weird artworks appeared.Duchamp's urinal, Fountain: Marcel Duchamp signed a porcelain urinal R. Mutt and submitted it to an exhibition, helping launch conceptual art.
When these weird artworks appeared.Mona Lisa with a moustache: Duchamp drew a moustache and goatee on a postcard of Leonardo's painting and titled it with a rude pun.
When these weird artworks appeared.This Is Not a Pipe: Magritte's famous painting shows a pipe with the French caption claiming it is not a pipe, because it is only a picture of one.
When these weird artworks appeared.Dalí's Lobster Telephone: Salvador Dalí made this surrealist sculpture with a lobster in place of a handset, a typical piece of his playful strangeness.
When these weird artworks appeared.Manzoni's canned Artist's Shit: Piero Manzoni claimed to have sealed his own excrement in 90 tin cans, sold for the price of their weight in gold.
When these weird artworks appeared.Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans: Andy Warhol painted 32 canvases, one for each flavour then sold, and made a mass-produced product into fine art.
When these weird artworks appeared.Hirst's shark in formaldehyde: Damien Hirst's tiger shark preserved in a tank, titled The Physical Impossibility of Death in the Mind of Someone Living, became a symbol of 1990s British art.
When these weird artworks appeared.Banksy's self-shredding art: A Banksy painting began shredding itself just after it sold at auction at Sotheby's, and was renamed Love Is in the Bin.
When these weird artworks appeared.Banana duct-taped to a wall: Maurizio Cattelan's Comedian was a real banana taped to a wall and sold for 120,000 dollars at Art Basel Miami Beach.

Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Hydrogen atom: It has one proton and one electron, and hydrogen makes up about three quarters of all ordinary matter in the universe.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Width of DNA: Each cell packs about two metres of DNA, coiled so tightly that it fits inside a nucleus smaller than a speck of dust.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Coronavirus: The name comes from Latin 'corona', crown, after the spiky halo of proteins seen under an electron microscope.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.E. coli bacterium: Most strains live harmlessly in your gut, and in ideal conditions one cell divides about every 20 minutes.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Red blood cell: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus and last about 120 days, and your body makes around two million every second.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Width of a human hair: Hair grows about a centimetre a month, and its width varies from person to person and across the scalp.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Grain of sand: Most beach sand is quartz, a form of silica, and sizes range from fine to coarse across about 0.06 to 2 mm.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Flea: It stores energy in a springy protein called resilin and can leap dozens of times its own body length.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.World's smallest frog: Paedophryne amauensis from Papua New Guinea was described in 2012, making it the smallest known vertebrate at the time.
Tiny, tinier, tiniest.Bee hummingbird: Cuba's bee hummingbird is the world's smallest bird, weighing under 2 g, with a heart that beats over a thousand times a minute.

Bizarre moments in history.Cadaver Synod (pope on trial): Pope Stephen VI had the rotting body of his predecessor Formosus dug up and put on trial. The verdict was later annulled.
Bizarre moments in history.War of the Bucket: Modena stole a wooden bucket from Bologna and won the resulting battle, and it still keeps the bucket in its tower.
Bizarre moments in history.Dancing Plague: In Strasbourg, hundreds danced for days, perhaps from stress, and authorities prescribed more dancing.
Bizarre moments in history.London Beer Flood: A vat burst at the Meux Brewery, sending a wave of porter through the streets and killing eight people.
Bizarre moments in history.The Great Stink: A hot summer made the Thames reek of sewage, and Parliament finally funded Bazalgette's sewer system.
Bizarre moments in history.Kentucky Meat Shower: Chunks of what looked like meat fell from a clear sky; later analysis suggested vultures' vomit.
Bizarre moments in history.Boston Molasses Flood: A tank burst and sent a wave of molasses through Boston's North End, killing 21 people.
Bizarre moments in history.The Great Emu War: Australian soldiers with machine guns tried to cull emus in Western Australia and largely failed.
Bizarre moments in history.Tanganyika laughter epidemic: It began at a girls' school in Kashasha and spread through villages, closing schools for months.
Bizarre moments in history.Oregon's exploding whale: Officials blew up a beached sperm whale in Florence with dynamite, and chunks of blubber rained down on spectators.

Games of skill, ancient to modern.Senet: Played in ancient Egypt and found in Tutankhamun's tomb, its rules were lost and have been reconstructed from clues.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Royal Game of Ur: Found in royal tombs at Ur, its rules were pieced together from a Babylonian tablet by British Museum curator Irving Finkel.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Go: Born in China as weiqi, it has more possible board positions than atoms in the universe, and AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Chaturanga (early chess): An early Indian ancestor of chess, with armies of infantry, cavalry, elephants and chariots.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Checkers: Called draughts in Britain, it was declared 'solved' in 2007: perfect play leads to a draw.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Scrabble: Alfred Butts invented it in the Depression, studying the front page of the New York Times to set letter frequencies.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Mastermind: Invented by Israeli telecom expert Mordecai Meirowitz, it was inspired by the older pencil-and-paper game Bulls and Cows.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Rubik's Cube: Ernő Rubik created it as a teaching tool, and it has about 43 quintillion possible positions.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Sudoku: Invented as 'Number Place' by American Howard Garns, it got its Japanese name and fame there. Sudoku means 'single number'.
Games of skill, ancient to modern.Tetris: Alexey Pajitnov created it at a Soviet computer center in Moscow, and the Game Boy version made it a worldwide phenomenon.

Some of the world's oldest businesses.Kongō Gumi (builders): Japanese temple builders operated for over 1,400 years until absorbed into another firm in 2006.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan: This Japanese hot spring inn in Yamanashi has used water from the same spring for over 1,300 years.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.St. Peter Stiftskeller: This Salzburg restaurant claims to be Europe's oldest, first mentioned in 803 by the scholar Alcuin.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.The Royal Mint: Britain's coin maker moved from the Tower of London to Wales between 1968 and 1975.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Weihenstephan brewery: This Bavarian brewery near Freising claims to be the oldest working one, and is part of the Technical University of Munich.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Stora Kopparberg mine: Sweden's Falun copper mine produced for centuries and shaped the nation's economy.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Beretta: This Italian gunmaker has been owned by the same family for roughly 500 years.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Zildjian cymbals: Founded by an Armenian alchemist in Constantinople with a secret alloy formula; now based in Massachusetts.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Hudson's Bay Company: Chartered by King Charles II, its Rupert's Land trading territory covered a huge share of what is now Canada.
Some of the world's oldest businesses.Twinings: London tea merchants Thomas Twining's shop at 216 Strand has stood on the site since 1706.

Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Toy Story: It was the first fully computer-animated feature film, and Pixar's team had to invent much of the software to make it.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Shrek: Chris Farley first recorded Shrek but died before finishing, so Mike Myers re-recorded the role with a Scottish accent.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Back to the Future: Eric Stoltz was originally cast as Marty and shot weeks of footage before Michael J. Fox replaced him.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Jurassic Park: Spielberg showed dinosaurs on screen for only about 15 minutes, using animatronics and early computer graphics for most of them.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).The Matrix: Filmed in Sydney, it popularised the 'bullet time' effect, in which the camera swirls around a frozen moment.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Pulp Fiction: A non-linear story that won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1994 and made John Travolta's dance scene famous.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Avatar: James Cameron's film is among the highest-grossing movies ever, and its Pandora scenes were largely made with motion capture.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).The Godfather: Marlon Brando won an Oscar for his role in it, and declined to accept the award, sending an activist to speak in his place.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Titanic: It won 11 Oscars, tying the record set by Ben-Hur, and its ship was rebuilt on a massive scale in Mexico.
Movie runtimes (theatrical cut).Gone with the Wind: Adjusted for inflation, it is the biggest box office hit ever, and it ran long enough to include an intermission.

When these crunchy snacks arrived.Triscuit: Made from whole wheat, it was introduced by the Shredded Wheat Company at Niagara Falls.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Cheez-It: It was created in Dayton, Ohio, by the Green and Green Company.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Fritos: Charles Elmer Doolin bought the recipe for a corn chip in San Antonio for $100.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Ritz crackers: Nabisco launched it in 1934, in the Depression, with a name chosen to suggest luxury.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Cheetos: Frito-Lay's Charles Elmer Doolin invented it in 1948, and it got a mascot, Chester Cheetah.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Ruffles: The ridges make them sturdy enough for dips, as the slogan promised.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Goldfish crackers (US): Margaret Rudkin of Pepperidge Farm found the fish-shaped cracker in Switzerland and introduced it in the US in 1962.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Pringles: Fred Baur designed the stackable can, and at his request his ashes were buried in one.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.SunChips: Frito-Lay's multigrain chips arrived in 1991; the compostable bag was famously loud.
When these crunchy snacks arrived.Takis: Takis are rolled tortilla chips from the Mexican company Barcel, and the name nods to taquitos.

US coins and bills, by value.Penny: Lincoln has been on the penny since 1909, and it now costs more than a cent to make.
US coins and bills, by value.Nickel: It is mostly copper, with 25 percent nickel.
US coins and bills, by value.Dime: It is the smallest and thinnest US coin, though worth more than the penny and nickel, and it bears Franklin Roosevelt.
US coins and bills, by value.Quarter: The state quarters program ran from 1999 to 2008.
US coins and bills, by value.Kennedy coin: Introduced shortly after the assassination of JFK in 1964.
US coins and bills, by value.Sacagawea coin: She was the Shoshone woman who guided Lewis and Clark, and the coin shows her with her infant son.
US coins and bills, by value.Lincoln bill: Lincoln has been on the five-dollar bill since 1914.
US coins and bills, by value.Hamilton bill: Alexander Hamilton, the first Treasury Secretary, stayed on the $10 after the musical's success.
US coins and bills, by value.Jackson bill: Andrew Jackson, who disliked paper money and banks, appears on the $20.
US coins and bills, by value.Franklin bill: Benjamin Franklin was never president, and the $100 bill has color-shifting ink.

Writers, by age at death.John Keats: Keats died of tuberculosis in Rome, and his epitaph reads Here lies one whose name was writ in water, a line he asked for himself.
Writers, by age at death.Percy Bysshe Shelley: Shelley drowned when his sailboat sank in a storm off Italy, and legend says his heart did not burn on the funeral pyre.
Writers, by age at death.Emily Brontë: Emily Brontë wrote just one novel, Wuthering Heights, and she died of tuberculosis a year after its publication under the name Ellis Bell.
Writers, by age at death.Lord Byron: Byron died of fever in Greece while supporting its war of independence, and he is still revered there as a national hero.
Writers, by age at death.Edgar Allan Poe: Poe's death in Baltimore remains mysterious: he was found delirious on a street, and the cause was never settled.
Writers, by age at death.Jane Austen: Jane Austen published four novels anonymously in her lifetime, and the readers of Sense and Sensibility knew the author as By a Lady.
Writers, by age at death.George Orwell: Orwell finished Nineteen Eighty-Four while seriously ill with tuberculosis on the remote Scottish island of Jura, and he died months after its release.
Writers, by age at death.William Shakespeare: Shakespeare died in Stratford, and he reportedly left his wife his second-best bed in his will, which has fascinated scholars for centuries.
Writers, by age at death.Charles Dickens: Dickens died in 1870 leaving The Mystery of Edwin Drood unfinished, and he was buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey.
Writers, by age at death.Leo Tolstoy: Tolstoy lived to 82, and in his last days he fled his estate by night, and died of pneumonia at a small railway station.

How long these short-lived states lasted.Carpatho-Ukraine: Declared independence on 15 March 1939 as Czechoslovakia fell apart, then was overrun by Hungarian troops within days.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Republic of West Florida: Settlers near Baton Rouge rebelled against Spain in 1810 and raised a lone-star flag, before the United States annexed the territory.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Republic of Ezo (Japan): Founded in 1869 by defeated shogunate loyalists on Hokkaido, it even held an election for its president, Enomoto Takeaki.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Biafra: Seceded from Nigeria in 1967; the civil war and blockade that followed caused a famine that killed perhaps over a million people.
How long these short-lived states lasted.United Arab Republic: Egypt and Syria merged under Nasser in 1958; Syria walked out in 1961, yet Egypt kept the name until 1971.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Kingdom of Westphalia: Napoleon created it for his younger brother Jerome in 1807, with Kassel as capital; it vanished after Napoleon's defeat at Leipzig in 1813.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Republic of Texas: Won independence from Mexico at the Battle of San Jacinto in 1836, then joined the US in 1845. Its Lone Star flag lives on as the state's.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Gran Colombia: Simon Bolivar's dream union of today's Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama broke apart by 1831 amid regional rivalries.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Vermont Republic: Had its own coins, post office and constitution before becoming the 14th US state in 1791, the first to join after the original 13.
How long these short-lived states lasted.Orange Free State: A Boer republic in southern Africa, annexed by Britain in 1900 during the Boer War; its capital, Bloemfontein, is now in South Africa.

Moments in plant history.Dutch tulip mania peaks: The speculative craze for tulip bulbs peaked in the Dutch Republic, though historians now think its scale was exaggerated.
Moments in plant history.Linnaeus's Species Plantarum: It set the starting point for modern plant naming, using a two-part Latin name for each species.
Moments in plant history.Kew Gardens founded: Founded by Princess Augusta, the botanical garden in London became a World Heritage Site.
Moments in plant history.Mutiny on the breadfruit ship: Captain Bligh's crew rebelled aboard the Bounty, which had been collecting breadfruit plants for the Caribbean.
Moments in plant history.Irish potato blight strikes: The potato disease triggered a famine in Ireland that killed around a million people and drove mass emigration.
Moments in plant history.Mendel publishes pea studies: The monk's results lay unnoticed for decades before being rediscovered in 1900 and founding the study of genetics.
Moments in plant history.First Chelsea Flower Show: The show began on the grounds of the Royal Hospital Chelsea, and it is now the world's most famous flower show.
Moments in plant history.Norway's first Trafalgar tree: Norway sends London a giant Christmas tree each year, a thank you for British help during the Second World War.
Moments in plant history.First GM tomato on sale: The Flavr Savr was designed to ripen slowly, but it was a commercial failure.
Moments in plant history.Svalbard Seed Vault opens: The vault holds over a million seed samples buried in a mountain in the Arctic, as insurance against disasters.

French kings, by when they took the thro.Clovis: Clovis united the Frankish tribes and converted to Catholic Christianity, shaping France's later ties to the Church.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Pepin the Short: He deposed the last Merovingian king and started the Carolingian dynasty, and was father of Charlemagne.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Charlemagne: Crowned Emperor in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800, he ruled much of western Europe.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Hugh Capet: He founded the Capetian dynasty, whose branches, including the Valois and Bourbons, ruled France for most of 800 years.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Philip Augustus: He expanded royal lands, built the Louvre as a fortress and joined Richard the Lionheart on the Third Crusade.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Saint Louis: Louis IX is the only French king to be canonised, and he died on crusade in Tunis.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Philip the Fair: He broke the Knights Templar in 1307 and fought the papacy, a feud that led to the popes' stay in Avignon.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Charles the Wise: Charles V rebuilt France during the Hundred Years' War, retook land from England and began building the Bastille.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Charles the Victorious: He ended the Hundred Years' War largely after Joan of Arc helped crown him at Reims.
French kings, by when they took the thro.Louis the Universal Spider: Louis XI earned his nickname for his scheming web of intrigues, preferring diplomacy to war.

Welsh numbers, by the value they name.un: Welsh traditionally counts in twenties, so 'forty' is literally 'two twenties', though a decimal system is now taught as well.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.dau: Dau is the masculine form; with feminine nouns it becomes dwy, so the gender of what you count changes the number word.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.tri: Tri also changes to tair with feminine nouns and, unusually, alters the first letter of some words that follow it.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.pedwar: Welsh pedwar is a cousin of Latin quattuor, since both descend from the same ancient root, and feminine nouns use pedair.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.pump: Pump shares a root with Greek pente; Celtic languages turned an old 'kw' sound into P where Latin kept it in quinque.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.chwech: Chwech is cognate with Latin sex and English six, with a Welsh ch sound like the one in the Scottish loch.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.saith: Saith is kin to Latin septem and English seven, and it is the number behind the Welsh word for a week.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.wyth: The Welsh word for week, wythnos, literally means 'eight nights', counting both ends of the week as the French do with huit jours.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.naw: Naw is a relative of English nine and Latin novem; the n-sound runs through almost all Indo-European words for nine.
Welsh numbers, by the value they name.deg: The word for 'eleven', un ar ddeg, literally means 'one on ten', and deg also gives degfed, 'tenth'.

Strange natural events, in order.The Year Without a Summer: Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption cooled the planet, with frost in New England in summer, and a gloomy Swiss summer pushed Mary Shelley to write Frankenstein.
Strange natural events, in order.Carrington solar storm: Auroras were seen as far south as the Caribbean, and telegraph operators got shocks, while some sent messages without batteries.
Strange natural events, in order.Great Blizzard of the US East: It dropped up to 50 inches of snow on the East Coast and brought down wires, helping to spur cities to bury cables and build subways.
Strange natural events, in order.Tunguska blast: A space rock blew up over remote Siberia, flattening some 80 million trees across about 2,000 square kilometres, yet left no crater.
Strange natural events, in order.Tri-State Tornado: The deadliest tornado in US history killed about 700 people along a track of over 350 kilometres through three states.
Strange natural events, in order.Black Sunday dust storm: A towering wall of dust swallowed the Great Plains in April, one of the worst storms of the Dust Bowl.
Strange natural events, in order.Lituya Bay megatsunami: A rockslide into an Alaskan bay launched a wave that ran up the hillside to about 520 metres, the tallest in modern history.
Strange natural events, in order.Lake Nyos gas cloud: A cloud of carbon dioxide burst from a crater lake in Cameroon, suffocating about 1,700 people and thousands of livestock overnight.
Strange natural events, in order.The Perfect Storm: A nor'easter merged with a hurricane's remains and sank the fishing boat Andrea Gail, a story told in Sebastian Junger's book.
Strange natural events, in order.Chelyabinsk meteor: A 20-metre asteroid exploded over Russia, and its shock wave shattered windows, injuring over a thousand people, mostly from flying glass.

Screen resolutions by pixel count.QVGA: The initials mean Quarter VGA, one quarter of the pixels, and it was typical for early smartphones and handheld organisers.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.VGA: Introduced by IBM in 1987, its 15-pin VGA connector survived on monitors and projectors for decades.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.SVGA: Super VGA's 800 by 600 became a standard for early websites, back when designers worried about screens being this small.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.XGA: Born as an IBM display standard in 1990, 1024 by 768 later became the resolution of projectors and the first iPad.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.HD Ready: A European label meaning a TV could show HD pictures but might need an external tuner, with 720 lines of pixels.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.Full HD: Its 1080 lines give about 2.07 million pixels, the standard of Blu-ray discs and most monitors for years.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.QHD: Quad HD is four times 720p, and 1440 lines made it popular on gaming monitors and flagship phones.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.4K UHD: Consumer UHD has four times the pixels of Full HD; cinema's 4K is slightly wider at 4096 by 2160.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.5K: At nearly 14.7 million pixels, Apple first used it on the 27-inch iMac with Retina display in 2014.
Screen resolutions by pixel count.8K UHD: At 33 million pixels, four times 4K, it was first broadcast by Japan's NHK in 2018, but there is little native content.

Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Frank Slide, Canada: A mountain face collapsed onto the Alberta town of Frank within moments, burying part of the town and a stretch of railway.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Wellington avalanche, USA: The deadliest avalanche in US history swept two trains off the tracks in Washington's Cascades, killing about 96 people.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Alps' Winter of Terror: Heavy snow across the Alps set off hundreds of avalanches over weeks, killing more than 200 people.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Vajont Dam landslide: A slide into a reservoir sent a giant wave over the dam; the dam itself held, yet about 2,000 people died below.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Huascarán (Yungay), Peru: An earthquake dislodged ice and rock from Peru's highest peak, burying the town of Yungay and killing about 20,000 people.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Sarno mudslides, Italy: After heavy rain, mud poured from the slopes above Sarno and nearby towns in Campania, killing over 150 people.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Galtür avalanche, Austria: A huge avalanche hit this Tyrolean village, killing 31 people in an area that was believed safe.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Kedarnath floods and slides: Extreme monsoon rain and a glacial lake burst devastated this Himalayan pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Oso landslide, Washington: A hillside collapsed onto a rural neighborhood, killing 43 people in the deadliest single landslide in US history.
Landslides, mudslides and avalanches, in.Rigopiano avalanche, Italy: An avalanche, set off after earthquakes, buried a mountain hotel in Abruzzo, killing 29 people.

When these medical devices first appeare.Eyeglasses: They likely began in northern Italy, and in 1306 a friar said they had been invented less than twenty years earlier.
When these medical devices first appeare.Compound microscope: Credit goes to Dutch spectacle makers Hans and Zacharias Janssen; Leeuwenhoek later saw bacteria with his own simple version.
When these medical devices first appeare.Stethoscope: René Laennec invented it using a rolled paper tube, partly from modesty about pressing his ear to a woman's chest.
When these medical devices first appeare.Hypodermic syringe: Alexander Wood in Edinburgh and Charles Pravaz in Lyon developed it around the same time.
When these medical devices first appeare.Blood pressure cuff: Scipione Riva-Rocci invented the cuff, and Korotkoff's sounds in 1905 let doctors read the lower number.
When these medical devices first appeare.Iron lung: Philip Drinker's tank used pressure to move air for polio patients, and some people lived in them for decades.
When these medical devices first appeare.Kidney dialysis machine: Willem Kolff built it in occupied Netherlands during World War II using sausage casing, juice cans and washing-machine parts.
When these medical devices first appeare.Defibrillator (on a human): Claude Beck first used it on a human in 1947, a 14-year-old boy whose heart was exposed during surgery.
When these medical devices first appeare.Implanted pacemaker: Swedish engineer Rune Elmqvist and surgeon Åke Senning made it, and patient Arne Larsson used 26 of them and lived to 86.
When these medical devices first appeare.LASIK eye surgery: It uses an excimer laser to reshape the cornea, and the laser was first made for etching computer chips.

Famous product flops, by launch year.Ford Edsel: Ford sank about $250 million into it, its horse-collar grille drew mockery, and it was dropped after three years.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Betamax: Sony's format arguably had better quality than VHS, but its shorter recording time cost it the market.
Famous product flops, by launch year.New Coke: It was pulled after just 79 days, as Coca-Cola reverted to Coca-Cola Classic following a backlash.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Crystal Pepsi: A clear cola with no coloring, backed by Super Bowl ads, it was revived briefly in 2015 and 2016.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Apple Newton: A pioneering handheld mocked for its faulty handwriting recognition, it was killed by Steve Jobs in 1998.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Segway: Hyped as the future of transport, it found a niche with mall guards and tour groups, and production ended in 2020.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Microsoft Zune: Microsoft's iPod rival had wireless sharing called squirting, and it was discontinued in 2012.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Google Glass: Wearers were nicknamed Glassholes, the consumer version was pulled in 2015, and it later found work in industry.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Juicero: The $400 juicer squeezed proprietary packs, until Bloomberg showed they could be squeezed by hand; it shut down in 2017.
Famous product flops, by launch year.Quibi: The short-form mobile video service raised $1.75 billion and shut down within about six months.

Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Breguet: Abraham-Louis Breguet invented the tourbillon and made watches for Marie Antoinette, one of which was finished after her death.
The Tiffany Blue Box, introduced in 1845, is a registered color of its own.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Patek Philippe: Its slogan says you never actually own one; the Henry Graves Supercomplication sold for $24 million in 2014.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Omega: The Speedmaster was the first watch on the Moon in 1969.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.TAG Heuer: Its Monaco model became famous on Steve McQueen's wrist in the 1971 film Le Mans.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Audemars Piguet: The Royal Oak, designed by Gérald Genta in 1972, with porthole-style bolts, was the first luxury steel sports watch.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Swarovski: Daniel Swarovski founded this Austrian crystal firm after inventing a machine for cutting crystal.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Rolex: Hans Wilsdorf founded it in London, picked a name easy to pronounce in any language, and made the first waterproof wristwatch in 1926.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Casio: Its G-Shock, begun in 1983, was designed to survive a fall from a three-story building.
Watch and jewelry houses, by founding ye.Swatch: Plastic watches that rescued the Swiss watch industry from the quartz crisis.

Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Giotto: Considered the father of Western painting for introducing lifelike volume; his Scrovegni Chapel frescoes in Padua survive.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Donatello: His bronze David was the first freestanding nude statue made since antiquity.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Sandro Botticelli: The Birth of Venus was painted for the Medici circle; he died in obscurity and was rediscovered in the 19th century.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Leonardo da Vinci: The Mona Lisa's painter and also an inventor, whose notebooks are written in mirror script.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Albrecht Dürer: The German master of printmaking painted a remarkable self-portrait at just 13.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Michelangelo: He painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling while insisting he was a sculptor, and carved the David from a flawed block.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Raphael: He died young, at 37, leaving behind the School of Athens fresco in the Vatican.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Pieter Bruegel the Elder: He painted peasants and proverbs, as in The Hunters in the Snow, and his sons Pieter and Jan also became painters.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.El Greco: Born in Crete and active in Spain, his elongated figures were rediscovered by modern artists.
Renaissance and Baroque artists, by birt.Caravaggio: He pioneered dramatic light and shadow, chiaroscuro, and fled Rome after killing a man in 1606.

Number of chromosomes.Jack jumper ant (female): Females of this Australian ant have just two chromosomes, the lowest known for any animal, and males have one. Its sting can trigger severe allergic reactions.
Number of chromosomes.Fruit fly: Thomas Hunt Morgan used these flies in the early 1900s to prove genes sit on chromosomes, earning a Nobel Prize in 1933. They have just four pairs.
Number of chromosomes.Garden pea: It has seven pairs, and Gregor Mendel's famous 1860s inheritance experiments tracked seven traits in pea plants, which launched modern genetics.
Number of chromosomes.Cat: Cats have 19 pairs. Calico and tortoiseshell cats are almost always female because the orange coat color gene sits on the X chromosome.
Number of chromosomes.Human: Humans have 23 pairs. Our chromosome 2 is a fusion of two ape chromosomes, which is why great apes have 48 and we have 46.
Number of chromosomes.Pineapple: Its crown can be cut off and replanted to grow a new plant. Pineapple has 50 chromosomes, 25 pairs, in its cells.
Number of chromosomes.Garden strawberry: The cultivated strawberry has eight sets of chromosomes, and it arose in 1700s France when two American species were grown side by side and crossed.
Number of chromosomes.Horse: Horses have 64, and a mule, the hybrid of a horse and a donkey, ends up with an odd 63 and is almost always sterile.
Number of chromosomes.Dog: Dogs have 78, the same as wolves, which is why the two can interbreed and have fertile offspring.
Number of chromosomes.Adder's-tongue fern: This small fern has the highest known chromosome count of any organism, though the number reflects repeated genome duplication, not complexity.

When these last rulers lost their throne.Cleopatra, last pharaoh: Egypt's last pharaoh was Greek by descent, from the Ptolemaic line, and was the first of her dynasty to learn Egyptian. She died in 30 BC after Octavian's victory.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Romulus Augustulus: The last Western Roman emperor, he was deposed as a teenager by the Germanic general Odoacer, and his nickname means "little Augustus". Historians date the fall of Rome to this.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Yazdegerd III of Persia: The last Sasanian king fled across Persia after defeats by the Arab armies, and was killed in 651, ending a dynasty that had lasted four centuries.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Emperor Ai of Tang: The last Tang emperor was forced to abdicate in favor of a warlord in 907, beginning the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Harold, last Anglo-Saxon king: Killed at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, and his death led to the Norman Conquest by William. Legend says he was struck in the eye with an arrow.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Al-Musta'sim, Abbasid caliph: The last Abbasid caliph of Baghdad was executed by the Mongols after they sacked the city in 1258, a disaster for Islamic scholarship.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Zhao Bing, last Song emperor: The child emperor of the Song dynasty died at the Battle of Yamen in 1279, when a minister jumped into the sea with him, ending the dynasty to the Mongols.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Toghon Temür of Yuan: The last Yuan emperor fled north when the Ming armies took Beijing in 1368. The Mongol dynasty founded by Kublai Khan had ruled China for about a century.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Constantine XI Palaiologos: The last Byzantine emperor died defending Constantinople in 1453 when the Ottomans, led by Mehmed II, took the city with huge cannons.
When these last rulers lost their throne.Boabdil of Granada: The last Muslim ruler of Granada surrendered the Alhambra to Ferdinand and Isabella in January 1492, ending nearly eight centuries of Muslim rule in Iberia.

Count the arms and tentacles.Elephant (trunks): Its trunk, fused from nose and upper lip, can uproot a tree or pick up a single peanut.
Count the arms and tentacles.Human (arms): Each arm and hand together hold 30 bones, which is why the wrist and hand are so dexterous.
Count the arms and tentacles.Garden snail (tentacles): The upper pair carry eyes at the tips and the lower pair smell and touch; a snail can regrow a damaged eyestalk.
Count the arms and tentacles.Starfish (common): They can regrow lost arms, and some can regrow an entire body from a single arm.
Count the arms and tentacles.Octopus: About two-thirds of its neurons are in its arms, and it has three hearts and blue blood.
Count the arms and tentacles.Squid: Squid have eight arms plus two longer tentacles used to snatch prey.
Count the arms and tentacles.Sunflower sea star: One of the largest sea stars, it can span nearly a metre and hunts sea urchins with thousands of tube feet.
Count the arms and tentacles.Box jellyfish: It has 24 eyes and is among the most venomous animals in the sea; its tentacles grow in clusters from each corner.
Count the arms and tentacles.Nautilus: A living fossil: its sucker-less tentacles reach from a shell whose chambers provide buoyancy.
Count the arms and tentacles.Lion's mane jellyfish: The largest known jellyfish, with tentacles that can trail over 30 metres, rivalling a blue whale's length.

When these coins were first minted.Lydian stater: Made of electrum, a natural gold-silver mix, in Lydia (now Turkey), which later issued pure gold coins under Croesus.
When these coins were first minted.Athenian owl: Its owl and Athena design was so trusted that 'owls to Athens' became an idiom, like 'coals to Newcastle'.
When these coins were first minted.Roman denarius: The silver coin's initial 'd' lived on as the abbreviation for the British penny until 1971.
When these coins were first minted.Gold solidus: Constantine introduced it; the word 'soldier' comes from this coin, in which soldiers were paid.
When these coins were first minted.Umayyad gold dinar: Abd al-Malik's reform put Arabic inscriptions rather than images on the coin, replacing the Byzantine design.
When these coins were first minted.Offa's silver penny: King Offa of Mercia's coin influenced English coinage for centuries, and the pound derived from a pound weight of silver pennies.
When these coins were first minted.Jiaozi paper money: Song-dynasty Sichuan printed what is often called the world's first government paper money.
When these coins were first minted.Florentine florin: Its name comes from the flower, the lily, on one side; it became a standard coin across Europe.
When these coins were first minted.Venetian ducat: Its gold content remained almost unchanged for about 500 years, so merchants trusted it.
When these coins were first minted.Tyrolean Guldengroschen: This silver coin was an ancestor of the thaler, which gave us the word 'dollar'.

When these toys first hit shelves.Mr. Potato Head: It was the first toy advertised on TV, and originally you used a real potato, which sometimes rotted.
When these toys first hit shelves.Play-Doh (as a toy): It started life as a wallpaper cleaner before it was marketed to children as modeling clay.
When these toys first hit shelves.Etch A Sketch: André Cassagnes invented it in France, using aluminium powder, and Ohio Art sold it worldwide.
When these toys first hit shelves.G.I. Joe: Hasbro coined the term 'action figure' to make dolls appeal to boys in the 1960s.
When these toys first hit shelves.Hot Wheels: Mattel's first set was the 'Sweet 16' cars, with metal tracks and fast wheels designed to roll.
When these toys first hit shelves.Cabbage Patch Kids: Customers 'adopted' each one with its own birth certificate and name, and a Christmas buying frenzy followed.
When these toys first hit shelves.Teddy Ruxpin: The animatronic bear moved its mouth and eyes to a cassette tape in his back, telling stories.
When these toys first hit shelves.Beanie Babies: Ty Warner deliberately limited supply and retired models, which fuelled a collecting craze.
When these toys first hit shelves.Tamagotchi: The name blends the Japanese for 'egg' and 'watch', and it was a virtual pet that needed constant care.
When these toys first hit shelves.Furby: Over 40 million sold in three years, and it seemed to learn English slowly from its own 'Furbish'.

When these file formats were introduced.GIF: The graphics format was introduced by CompuServe, and its creators say it is pronounced with a soft g, like 'jif', though most people disagree.
When these file formats were introduced.ZIP: Phil Katz made it for compressing files, and its name suggests speed, and it has an open-source format.
When these file formats were introduced.JPEG: The image format, named after the Joint Photographic Experts Group, compresses by discarding detail the eye is least likely to notice.
When these file formats were introduced.PDF: Adobe created this document format so that files look the same everywhere, and it stands for Portable Document Format.
When these file formats were introduced.PNG: Created as a free alternative to GIF, it supports transparency, and the name stands for Portable Network Graphics.
When these file formats were introduced.JSON: The data format is based on JavaScript, and Douglas Crockford named it, and it has become the common format for web data.
When these file formats were introduced.DOCX: Microsoft Word changed to a zipped XML format, and the file is actually a ZIP archive that you can open.
When these file formats were introduced.WebP: Google created this image format, based on video, and it is smaller than JPEG and PNG.
When these file formats were introduced.HEIC (as iPhone default): Apple chose this format for photos as it saves about half the space, and it has caused compatibility issues.
When these file formats were introduced.AVIF: The format from the Alliance for Open Media is based on the AV1 video codec, and it is royalty-free.

Animals in space, in order.Fruit flies on a V-2: A US V-2 launch carried the first animals into space, and the flies were recovered alive.
Animals in space, in order.Albert II the monkey: This rhesus monkey was launched on a V-2 and reached space, but died on impact when the parachute failed.
Animals in space, in order.Laika the dog: She was the first animal in orbit aboard Sputnik 2, and she died within hours of overheating.
Animals in space, in order.Belka and Strelka: These two Soviet dogs were the first animals to orbit and return alive, and one of Strelka's puppies went to the Kennedys.
Animals in space, in order.Ham the chimpanzee: Trained to pull levers for banana pellets, he flew on Mercury before Alan Shepard did and survived.
Animals in space, in order.Félicette the cat: France sent this cat on a short suborbital flight in 1963, and she returned safely.
Animals in space, in order.Tortoises around the Moon: Zond 5 carried two Russian tortoises plus insects, and they were the first creatures to fly around the Moon and return.
Animals in space, in order.Arabella the spider: Skylab's spider spun an uneven web at first, then better ones as she adapted to weightlessness.
Animals in space, in order.Jellyfish on the Shuttle: The jellyfish bred in orbit, but their space-born offspring had trouble adapting to gravity back on Earth.
Animals in space, in order.Tardigrades exposed to space: These tiny creatures survived ten days of vacuum and radiation in a 2007 European experiment.

Man-made materials, by when they were in.Parkesine: Alexander Parkes created it, the first man-made plastic, from cellulose nitrate, and showed it at the 1862 London International Exhibition.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Celluloid: John Wesley Hyatt developed celluloid as a substitute for ivory in billiard balls, and it later became photographic film.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Rayon: Rayon, called artificial silk, is made from wood pulp cellulose, and was first made commercially by Hilaire de Chardonnet.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Cellophane: Swiss chemist Jacques Brandenberger invented it after seeing wine spill on a tablecloth, and wanting a waterproof cloth.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Stainless steel: Harry Brearley of Sheffield found it while seeking rust-resistant rifle barrels; chromium makes it stainless.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Polyethylene: This is the world's most common plastic, discovered by accident in 1933 at ICI in England.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Teflon: Roy Plunkett found Teflon by accident at DuPont, and almost nothing sticks to its slippery surface.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Styrofoam: Styrofoam is a brand name for Dow's building insulation foam; disposable cups are usually a different polystyrene foam.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Kevlar: Stephanie Kwolek invented it at DuPont, and by weight it is about five times stronger than steel, ideal for body armor.
Man-made materials, by when they were in.Carbon nanotubes: Sumio Iijima's discovery of these carbon tubes, only nanometers wide, kicked off nanotechnology; they are very strong for their weight.

Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Raleigh: Founded in Nottingham, this company became one of the world's biggest bicycle makers; its 1970 Chopper was a childhood icon.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Schwinn: The Chicago firm popularized balloon-tyre cruiser bikes and filed for bankruptcy in 1992.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Harley-Davidson: William Harley and the Davidson brothers built their first motorbike in a small Milwaukee shed; the company is still headquartered there.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Moto Guzzi: Based at Mandello del Lario in Italy, its eagle emblem honours the founders' air-force background.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Ducati: This Bologna firm began making radio components before motorbikes, and is known for desmodromic valves.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Yamaha Motor: It was spun off from the Yamaha musical-instrument company, which is why the logo features tuning forks.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Specialized: Mike Sinyard's California firm launched the Stumpjumper in 1981, one of the first mass-produced mountain bikes.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Trek: It began in a barn in Waterloo, Wisconsin, and grew into one of the world's biggest bicycle brands.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Peloton: It pairs exercise bikes with live-streamed classes, and demand surged during the 2020 pandemic lockdowns.
Bike and motorbike brands, by founding.Lime scooters: It began as LimeBike in 2017 with dockless bikes, and the green scooters later spread across cities.

When these music magazines launched.Billboard: It began as a trade paper for billposters, and later became the home of the US music charts.
When these music magazines launched.Gramophone: Compton Mackenzie founded it as a gramophone-record review, and it is still around as a leading classical review.
When these music magazines launched.Melody Maker: A jazz-focused weekly in its first years, it merged into NME in 2000.
When these music magazines launched.NME: The New Musical Express printed the first UK singles chart in 1952.
When these music magazines launched.Rolling Stone: Founded in San Francisco by Jann Wenner and Ralph Gleason, its first cover featured John Lennon.
When these music magazines launched.Kerrang!: The name mimics the sound of a power chord, and it started as a one-off supplement of the paper Sounds.
When these music magazines launched.Spin: Bob Guccione Jr. started it as a rival to Rolling Stone, aimed at younger music fans.
When these music magazines launched.Q: Mark Ellen and David Hepworth launched it with a five-star rating system, and it closed in 2020.
When these music magazines launched.Vibe: Quincy Jones helped to found this magazine, which covered hip-hop and R&B.
When these music magazines launched.Pitchfork: The Chicago site, set up by Ryan Schreiber, became so influential that Conde Nast bought it in 2015.

Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Speedo: Speedo took its name from a 1928 slogan, 'Speed on in your Speedos', coined when the Australian knitting firm moved into swimwear.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Lacoste: René Lacoste's nickname 'the Crocodile' became the brand's logo, and he created the tennis polo shirt after wearing it on court.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Ray-Ban Aviator: Built for US military pilots to cut high-altitude glare, its teardrop lenses were designed to cover the whole field of view.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Canada Goose: The Toronto company began as Metro Sportswear and later renamed itself after its goose-down parkas, made for extreme cold.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Dr. Martens boot: The name 1460 comes from its first release date, 1 April 1960. The air-cushioned sole came from a German doctor's skiing injury.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.UGG: Australian surfers wore sheepskin boots to warm up after cold waves. Founder Brian Smith brought the look to California in 1978.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Hermès Birkin bag: Actress Jane Birkin sketched her ideal travel bag for Hermès's chief executive on a flight, and the bag took her name.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Spanx: Sara Blakely launched it with about $5,000 of savings, after cutting the feet off pantyhose to wear under white pants.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Crocs: Crocs debuted at a Florida boat show as a boating shoe. The foam resin it's made of is called Croslite.
Fashion brands and icons, by debut year.Allbirds: Its first shoe used New Zealand merino wool, a fabric far more at home in sweaters than in sneakers.

How long these famous figures lived.Edward V of England: Edward V was one of the Princes in the Tower, who vanished in 1483 and were never seen again.
How long these famous figures lived.Joan of Arc: She was burned at the stake in 1431 and was declared a saint in 1920.
How long these famous figures lived.Alexander the Great: He died in Babylon in 323 BC, having conquered an empire that stretched to India.
How long these famous figures lived.Cleopatra: The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt was Greek by descent, and the first of her family to learn Egyptian.
How long these famous figures lived.Alfred the Great: He is the only English monarch to be called 'the Great', for resisting Viking invasions.
How long these famous figures lived.Julius Caesar: He was killed on the Ides of March in 44 BC, stabbed 23 times by senators.
How long these famous figures lived.Hannibal: The Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with elephants, and later took poison to avoid being captured.
How long these famous figures lived.Augustus: Rome's first emperor lived to 75, and the month of August is named after him.
How long these famous figures lived.Plato: He founded the Academy in Athens, taught by Socrates and in turn teaching Aristotle.
How long these famous figures lived.Ramesses II: He reigned for 66 years and fathered over a hundred children, and his mummy was given a passport to travel to Paris.

Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Fennec fox: The smallest fox has huge ears, up to about 15 cm long, that shed heat in the Sahara.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Chihuahua: The world's smallest dog breed is named after a Mexican state, and some have a soft spot in the skull like a baby.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Arctic fox: Its coat changes from white in winter to brown in summer, and it endures temperatures near minus 50 C.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Red fox: The most widespread wild carnivore, found across the entire Northern Hemisphere.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Beagle: Bred to hunt hares, its nose is so good that beagles inspect luggage at airports for forbidden food.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Coyote: It thrives in cities from Chicago to Los Angeles and can run about 40 mph.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.African wild dog: Hunting in packs, they succeed more often than lions, and each animal's coat pattern is unique.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Gray wolf: All domestic dogs descend from an ancient population of wolves, but it is a cousin rather than the direct ancestor.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.Great Dane: The record-holding Zeus stood over a meter tall at the shoulder, taller than many tables.
Dogs and their wild cousins by weight.English mastiff: A mastiff named Zorba holds the record for the heaviest dog, weighing well over 300 pounds.

Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Ox: The X tile is worth eight points, and 'ox' is one of the shortest ways to cash it in.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Qi: Accepted in Scrabble dictionaries, this Chinese word for life energy helps players dump a Q without needing a U.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Zany: It comes from the Italian 'zanni', the comic servants of Commedia dell'arte, and it puts a 10-point Z to use.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Jinx: It may come from 'jynx', a bird used in witchcraft, and combines the 8-point J and X.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Zephyr: From Zephyros, the Greek god of the west wind, it is a gentle breeze in poetry.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Quartz: Quartz is one of the most abundant minerals in Earth's crust, and its crystals keep time in watches.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Syzygy: An alignment of three celestial bodies, as at new or full moon, it packs in a Z and two Ys, plus no vowel besides Y.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Quixotic: The word comes from Cervantes's Don Quixote, and means idealistic and impractical.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Bezique: A trick-taking card game of French origin, said to be a favourite of Winston Churchill.
Scrabble face value of these tile-hoarde.Muzjiks: A rare plural of an old spelling of Russian peasant that lets you use J, Z, K and M in one play.

Underwater inventions, in order.Drebbel's submarine: Cornelis Drebbel, a Dutch inventor, tested a rowed submarine in the Thames. It reportedly carried passengers, even King James I.
Underwater inventions, in order.Halley's diving bell: Edmond Halley, of the comet, designed a diving bell that was resupplied with air from weighted barrels lowered from the surface.
Underwater inventions, in order.Turtle submarine: The Turtle, a one-man hand-cranked submarine, tried to attach a bomb to a British warship during the American Revolution.
Underwater inventions, in order.Siebe's diving helmet: Augustus Siebe's closed diving dress, with a helmet bolted to a waterproof suit, became the basis of standard diving gear for 100 years.
Underwater inventions, in order.Whitehead torpedo: Robert Whitehead's self-propelled torpedo was a naval game changer, and navies around the world soon bought his design.
Underwater inventions, in order.Beebe's bathysphere record: William Beebe and Otis Barton descended in a steel sphere to 923 m off Bermuda, farther than any human had gone before.
Underwater inventions, in order.Aqua-Lung: Jacques Cousteau and Emile Gagnan created the Aqua-Lung, the first successful open-circuit scuba, freeing divers from hoses to the surface.
Underwater inventions, in order.Wetsuit: The wetsuit was invented by physicist Hugh Bradner, who realized trapped neoprene bubbles could keep a diver warm in cold water.
Underwater inventions, in order.USS Nautilus launched: The first nuclear-powered submarine could stay submerged for weeks and crossed under the North Pole in 1958.
Underwater inventions, in order.Jet Ski: Kawasaki's Jet Ski made personal watercraft popular. The name is a brand, though people now use it for any such craft.

From sap to maple syrup.Wait for frosty nights: Sap flows best when nights are below freezing and days above, usually in late winter. The pressure changes drive it through the tree.
From sap to maple syrup.Drill a hole in a maple: Sugar maples are the main source of syrup, and a healthy tree isn't harmed by tapping. Producers take only a small portion of its sap.
From sap to maple syrup.Tap in a spout: The spout, or spile, is gently tapped into the hole, and the sap flows out. Traditional spouts were once carved from wood by Indigenous peoples.
From sap to maple syrup.Hang a bucket: Indigenous peoples of North America were the first to make maple syrup. Many modern producers use plastic tubing instead of buckets.
From sap to maple syrup.Sap drips in: Fresh sap is clear and only slightly sweet, about 2 per cent sugar. It tastes like faintly sweet water.
From sap to maple syrup.Haul sap to the sugar shack: The small wooden building where it is boiled is called a sugar shack, or cabane à sucre in Quebec, which is the world's top syrup producer.
From sap to maple syrup.Boil away most of the water: It takes about 40 litres of sap to make just one litre of syrup. The boiling turns the clear liquid golden and concentrates the sugar.
From sap to maple syrup.Filter the hot syrup: Filtering removes sugar sand, or niter, mineral crystals that would make the syrup cloudy. It's done while the syrup is still hot.
From sap to maple syrup.Pour into bottles: Syrup is bottled hot to seal and preserve it. It is graded by colour, from golden and delicate to very dark and robust.
From sap to maple syrup.Drizzle on pancakes: Pancakes with syrup are a classic North American breakfast. Real maple syrup is very different from the cheaper pancake syrups, which are mostly corn syrup.

Toy Story, in story order.Andy's birthday party: Toy Story (1995) was the first full-length feature film made entirely with computer animation.
Toy Story, in story order.Buzz Lightyear arrives: Buzz Lightyear is named in honour of astronaut Buzz Aldrin, and Tim Allen voiced him.
Toy Story, in story order.Buzz falls out the window: To infinity and beyond is Buzz's famous catchphrase, and his falling with style flight is the film's best joke.
Toy Story, in story order.Stranded at a gas station: The Pizza Planet truck has appeared as an Easter egg in nearly every Pixar film.
Toy Story, in story order.Pizza Planet claw machine: The squeaky aliens in the claw machine, worshipping the claw, became an early Pixar cult favourite.
Toy Story, in story order.Sid takes them home: Randy Newman's You've Got a Friend in Me was nominated for an Oscar, and he wrote the film's songs.
Toy Story, in story order.Buzz sees his TV commercial: Buzz thinks he's a real space ranger, and the 2022 film Lightyear imagined the movie that toy was supposedly based on.
Toy Story, in story order.Sid's toys come to the rescue: Sid's mutant toys, built from broken parts, are a creepy highlight that shows how the damaged toys are secretly kind.
Toy Story, in story order.Rocket ride to the moving van: The firework rocket carries Woody and Buzz to the van, and Buzz's wings finally pop open as he falls with style.
Toy Story, in story order.A puppy on Christmas morning: The Christmas puppy is the final gag, and it sets up the 1999 sequel.

How a US president is chosen.Candidates announce: The Constitution requires presidents to be at least 35, natural-born citizens and residents of the US for 14 years.
How a US president is chosen.First primaries: Iowa's caucuses and New Hampshire's primary are traditionally the first contests, giving small states outsized influence on who wins.
How a US president is chosen.Super Tuesday: Super Tuesday is when many states vote on the same day, and it often hands a front-runner an almost unbeatable lead in delegates.
How a US president is chosen.Party conventions: At the conventions delegates formally nominate their candidate, and the nominee usually reveals a running mate just before.
How a US president is chosen.Presidential debates: The first televised presidential debate pitted Kennedy against Nixon in 1960, and people who watched often felt Kennedy won.
How a US president is chosen.Election Day: Election Day has been held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November since an 1845 law, partly to fit farmers' schedules.
How a US president is chosen.Victory speech: The losing candidate's concession speech is tradition, not law, and it helps reassure the country that the transfer of power is peaceful.
How a US president is chosen.Electors cast their votes: There are 538 electors in all, and a candidate needs 270 of them to win, which is why the popular vote does not always decide it.
How a US president is chosen.Congress counts the votes: Congress counts the electoral votes in a joint session on January 6, and the vice president presides over that count.
How a US president is chosen.Inauguration Day: Inauguration Day has been January 20 since the 20th Amendment, ratified in 1933, took effect in 1937; before that it was in March.
